detail.longDescription: I have a directory [edit: Apparently "repository" isn't the correct word for this?] that has been fully-local for a few years [edit: To be clear, I haven't had this going online in any way that I could use as a reasonably up to date backup] and want to use [see also: introduce] GitHub as a sort of "backup" system [edit: TO BE CLEAR: I have only been doing offline backups, I want to be able to stop making local duplicates of this project and have the backup be a constantly evolving online snapshot, so If I somehow lose access to my offline copy, I have something reasonably recent to return to] . So far, I've managed to get my full [directory? repository? project?] uploaded to GH and I've figured out how to make VSCode log in to my GitHub account to see and edit the online copy. That's all fine, but what I want to be able to do is edit my existing local copy (That is, the same directory of files I have been working in since 2022, NOT the dupe of it I recently made on GitHub), and send my changes to the GitHub version of the project without having to manually open the site in my browser and re-upload the files in <100 file groups. As it is, I would need to manually keep re-uploading my files every time I make changes locally, and since this project involves folders containing more than 100 files each, uploading gets REALLY tedious really fast. In short: I have a local project that I have been working for years, but I am making a new remote version of it at GitHub (which was successfully set up already) and I intend to use this new remote as a security copy. I'm facing difficulties in pushing my changes to the new repo due to being new to how this works.
